summary.headline: SKF India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR 5.9 billion, with EBITDA flat YoY and up 540 bps QoQ.
summary.overview: Revenue reached INR 5.9 billion, up 27% YoY and down 1% QoQ, while sales of products were INR 5.5 billion, up about 22% YoY and down 0.7% QoQ. Growth was volume-led (+22% YoY) with price/mix adding 5.6% on a QoQ basis. EBITDA was broadly flat YoY (+7 bps) and up 540 bps QoQ as one-off demerger-related factors in Q4 FY26 faded. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to close to 20%, versus the earlier ~12% guidance, and said the ~17% margin is a normalised level for the next two years. Capex of about INR 500 crore is planned, with INR 170-180 crore expected this year.

financial_highlights.change: About 1% lower YoY; about 6.5% higher QoQ
About 60 bps higher YoY; about 650 bps higher QoQ (about 527 bps QoQ excluding Q4 exceptional items)

segments.name: OEM
segments.commentary: About 62% of Q1 sales. Within OEM: 2-wheelers ~54%, passenger vehicles ~31%, commercial vehicles ~15%. Management said historical ranges are 48-52%, 28-30% and 11-12% respectively.

segments.name: Vehicle aftermarket (distribution)
segments.commentary: About 20% of sales. Volumes plateaued or declined slightly; discounts given in the last two months are not expected to continue.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 8% of sales, up from about 6% QoQ; management said export is not a major strategic focus and expects it to stay in this range.

segments.name: SKF Industrial
segments.commentary: About 10% of sales. Management said it is non-core and expected to decline over the next few years, with capacity redirected to automotive customers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected close to 20%, above the earlier ~12% guidance; management said capacity is sufficient for this.
Gross margin expected to stay within the historical normal range, with quarterly variation from mix, seasonality and inventory revaluation (FIFO).
Margins around 17% expected to be the normal range for the next two years, per management confirmation.
Commodity-linked price increases under negotiation with OEMs; realisation lag of 1-2 quarters; amount not disclosed.
Revenue impact of new Haridwar capacity expected in FY28, not FY27.
Portfolio rationalisation (plants and loss-making businesses) expected to have no major impact on FY27.
capex_capacity: Capex plan of about INR 500 crore; about INR 170-180 crore expected in FY27; largely complete by FY28, with some spill into FY29.
Haridwar capacity additions to start in Q4 CY2026, with ramp-up taking time; growth impact in FY28. Mainly for 2-wheeler traction motor EV components, with some driveline.
Capacity is also being added through cycle-time and efficiency gains, with about 5 million pieces unlocked this year via technology upgrades.
Three plants (Pune, Bangalore, Haridwar) report over 98% renewable energy sourcing; Bangalore and Haridwar report water positivity.
demand_pricing: Macro: IIP grew 4.8% in Q1 FY27; manufacturing PMI 54.4 in June 2026; 2W and 3W production trending up, while PV and CV declined marginally; iron and steel output fell.
OEM contracts carry index-linked commodity clauses; a recent round of commodity-inflation pass-through is under discussion, amount not disclosed.
Price/mix contributed +5.6% QoQ to sales; some discounting in aftervehicle market in the last two months, to be discontinued.
Aftermarket competition includes many players and fake products; management is prioritising margin protection over volume.
Won a wheel-end business from a large PV manufacturer seeking localised bearing supply, starting Q4 CY2028.
EV non-wheel business: developmental platforms winning orders; production ramp-up from mid-FY27 and full visibility in 2028; revenue not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What drove sequential gross margin movement (51% vs 42.5% in Q4) and what commodity inflation and price hikes were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited mix, seasonality and FIFO inventory revaluation as drivers. Commodity pass-through is a work in progress with OEMs, with a 1-2 quarter lag; the amount was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~27% growth moderating, and is capacity sufficient?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 revenue growth close to 20%, versus ~12% earlier guidance. Capacity is at about 93% loading; the 20% target is covered by efficiency gains and new Haridwar capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Will INR 170-180 crore of capex come online this year, and is it backward or growth capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the Haridwar capacity starts in Q4 CY2026. It mainly reduces dependence on SKF Industrial trading volumes and is secondarily for growth; growth impact comes in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~17% margin normalised for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed this is the expected range.

qa_highlights.question: Will related-party trading with SKF Industrial pressure margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trading involves sales and purchases with SKF Industrial at a mark-up; margins should improve as own production capacity builds up.

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines and sizing of EV orders, and how much EV non-wheel revenue is there?
qa_highlights.answer: Developmental platforms will start production around Q4 CY2028; ramp-up from mid-2027. Management declined to quantify revenue or market share.

risks_watch: Vehicle aftermarket volumes plateaued or declined; recovery plan over the next five months is unquantified.
Commodity inflation pass-through timing and amount remain undisclosed, with a 1-2 quarter lag.
Gross margin volatility from mix, FIFO inventory revaluation and related-party trading with SKF Industrial.
EV revenue timing depends on developmental platforms ramping from 2027-2028; no quantified revenue yet.
Q4 CY2026 Haridwar capacity start and ramp-up timing are key for FY28 growth.
Capex of INR 500 crore plan with timing slippage risk into FY29.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the top line and margins, citing strong YoY growth and normalised profitability. Guidance was cautious on exports and aftermarket, and management was evasive on commodity pass-through amounts, Q1 capex and EV revenue quantification.
key_quotes: We expect the revenue growth to be in the range close to 20%, right, much better than the 12% guidance we had given earlier, around 20% something.
Our segment is purely automotive. Industrial, we are supplying where the industrial doesn't have capacity or something.
Largely, if you look at FY basis, largely it would be over by FY28. Maybe some part could spill down to FY29, but largely it will be over by FY28.
